Why Harlingen businesses miss calls

Harlingen is home to Valley International Airport and major medical providers, and education and health care employ almost 32% of workers. Seasonal Winter Texans add a yearly wave of older English-speaking customers, while about half of residents speak Spanish at home. That means the same clinic or repair shop may need two very different phone styles. A human receptionist cannot always cover both at busy times.

Which Harlingen businesses benefit most?

  • Medical offices: Serve Spanish speakers and Winter Texans alike.
  • Dental offices: Book seasonal visitors before they leave.
  • Auto repair shops: Answer RV and car calls while your team works.

Can you keep your Harlingen phone number?

Yes. Harlingen callers will usually see the 956 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Forward it to the AI for all calls, only after hours, or only when your team does not pick up. We can also set up a new local number. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
